implementation_notes: net/http makes the interception layer a decorator: `func validate(next http.Handler) http.Handler` returns a handler that inspects the request and either writes the rejection (http.Error/400) or calls `next.ServeHTTP`. Compose the decorator with a `http.ServeMux` (Go 1.22 pattern routing) and wrap the mux once at startup so every registered route is covered; middleware functions replace interceptor classes and no framework is required. Keep the rules in a separate package as pure functions of the request so they can be unit-tested without an HTTP server, and prefer wrapping the single mux over per-route wrapping.
pitfalls: Handlers registered on http.DefaultServeMux or on a mux built without the decorator bypass validation; construct exactly one wrapped mux and pass it everywhere.
Reading r.Body during validation leaves the handler at EOF unless the body is restored (`r.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(buf))`) or the handler reads from the buffered copy.
A decorator that writes the error response but still calls next produces a double write (superfluous WriteHeader); return immediately after rejecting.
